summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, he studied under teachers including Tertön Sogyal (~1895–1926) and Agvan Dorzhiev (~1898–1910). He taught many figures, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and the 9th Panchen Lama.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 1st Beru Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He taught numerous students, including Reginald A. Ray, 2nd Beru Khyentse, and Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, Khangsar Dorje Chang, and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under traditional teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, 41st Sakya Trizin, and Dilgo Khyentse.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Khenpo Appey and Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen. His students include Steven Neal Weinberger, Sam van Schaik, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, and 2nd Beru Khyentse.
He studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
Active in Indology, he studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1907–1911). He held posts at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).

Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he studied at the University of Madras (~1923–1927). He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1970).
An Indologist, he served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.

Active in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he earned a PhD from Stony Brook University under Sung Bae Park. He held posts at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).
Active in Indology and religious studies, he studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1971–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

Active in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987) and founded BJIAS in 1987.

A linguist and Indologist, he earned his Master's at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and PhD at Indiana University. He spent decades at the University of Chicago (1962–1983+) and held a visiting professorship at Harvard University (~1987–1988).
A linguist and Indologist, he completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore.

Active in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he studied at Columbia University and Halle. He held academic posts at Columbia University (fellow 1883–1886; professor 1895–1935) and was Corresponding Secretary of the American Oriental Society (1908).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he studied at the University of Colorado and completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (~2009–2015). In ~2015, he became an assistant professor of Japanese Studies at University at Albany, SUNY.

Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Government College of Art & Craft. He held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, he earned his PhD from Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and Ahmad Hasan Dani. He was an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

An Indologist and linguist, he studied under Michel Bréal and Éugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877), Sorbonne University (1877), and the University of Paris (~1885–1888), teaching Sylvain Lévi.

An Indologist who studied under Rambhadracharya, he served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, head of Sanskrit at Himachal Pradesh University, and visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.
